title: Stage 1: Raw data and a staging schema
summary: Profile a messy export and design the table clean data will land in.

steps.title: The brief
body: Rosa's last assignment isn't a case. It's a **build**. Larkspur's directors want one reliable dashboard of Inkwell & Ivy's sales, and right now all there is is a nightly CSV export dumped into a table called `raw_orders`.
You'll build a small **analytics warehouse** in four layers, the same shape real data teams use:
Raw       raw_orders                      exactly what the source sent, never edited
Model     dim_customer, dim_book,         a star schema built for questions
Reports   views + indexes                 what the dashboard reads
Each stage starts with the database as the previous stage left it. Stage 1: understand the raw data, then design the staging table.

steps.title: Profile the raw data
prompt: Before cleaning anything, measure the mess. Return one row with:
- **line_items**: distinct (`order_ref`, `isbn`) pairs: the real number of order lines
Tables: `raw_orders(order_ref, order_date, customer_email, customer_name, isbn, title, qty, unit_price, channel)`: every column is text, exactly as exported.
setup: CREATE TABLE raw_orders (order_ref TEXT, order_date TEXT, customer_email TEXT, customer_name TEXT, isbn TEXT, title TEXT, qty TEXT, unit_price TEXT, channel TEXT);

steps.explain: 15 rows but only 13 real lines: the exporter sent some lines twice. Four dates are in UK format and nine prices carry a pound sign. All of this has to be fixed on the way in.

steps.prompt: Which problem does each raw value show?
items: the same order line exported twice

steps.prompt: Why keep `raw_orders` untouched instead of cleaning it in place?
options: So any cleaning bug can be fixed and the load re-run from the original data
Because UPDATE is slower than INSERT
Raw tables can't be updated in SQLite
So the dashboard can read it directly
steps.explain: The raw layer is your source of truth. Staging is disposable: drop it, fix the query, rebuild.

steps.title: Designing the staging table
body: Staging is where data gets **real types and real rules**. Every constraint you add is a bug the database will refuse on your behalf:
- money as **integer cents** (`unit_cents`), never floating point
- a fixed set of channels: `CHECK (channel IN ('web', 'shop'))`
- a primary key on the **natural key** of an order line, `(order_ref, isbn)`, so duplicates can't get in
If a future export contains something new and weird, the load fails loudly instead of quietly poisoning the dashboard.

steps.title: Create stg_orders
solution: channel TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (channel IN ('web', 'shop')),
setup: CREATE TABLE raw_orders (order_ref TEXT, order_date TEXT, customer_email TEXT, customer_name TEXT, isbn TEXT, title TEXT, qty TEXT, unit_price TEXT, channel TEXT);

hints: Three CHECK constraints: qty, unit_cents and channel.
The composite key goes on its own line: `PRIMARY KEY (order_ref, isbn)`.
